sections.overall: Again, the best match of the week featured Darby Allin - another excellent showcase for the Men's main champ. His main event World Title match against Brody King on Dynamite (rated 8.48) helped him rise to #2 in the ranks. On Collision, Jack Perry pulled out his best one-on-one match (7.79) since Full Gear '22 with his National Title defense against Mascara Dorada. All his other top matches have typically been in multi-men contests. One to watch to see if he can produce more high-quality singles matches.
sections.mens: For the first time since 2022, Jon Moxley heads up the Men's rankings. I would never have predicted that a year ago! It his consistency rather than spectacular (i.e. rated over 9) match ratings this year, plus other big names (e.g. Fletcher and Page) dropping out recently to help him get there. But with Darby, Ospreay and others on the rise, how long will he stay there? Kevin Knight had two big title wins, but gained little overall as although the Dynamite one vs MJF (rated 7.79) gained more than the Collision main event against Hook (6.29), his already-high early 120s means only a small gain this week.
sections.womens: Welcome back Kris Statlander., not that she was out of the rankings for long! It was only a matter of time that she had a match longer than 5 minutes, which was eligble for the ratings and means she has re-entered at number 1. -Although Thekla's number 1 spot was brief, don't count her out reclaiming this at some point in 2026. Also, a long-awaited return for Anna Jay. Her TBS title match against Willow Nightingale on Collision (5.15) led to a minor rating points loss for both wrestlers. Hopefully Anna gets more opportunities - something that has been a systemic issue in the Women's Division for some time now.
sections.menstag: Several well-tenured teams (RPG Vice, Top Flight and Castagnoli & Moxley) re-entered the rankings this week, but not to trouble the Top 5. Although Cage & Copeland had their weakest match so far (rated 5.77), their upcoming World Tag Title match against FTR could launch them much further up.
sections.womenstag: The champions, Divine Dominion, have now a more reflective rating, after that disappointing title match at Revolution set them back. Their match rating of 6.9 was their best since their debut in March. With very few teams ranked, moving to #2 is a positive step in their surely inevitable rise to number 1. Their rating still clearly does not match their dominance presented on screen, but this is finally starting to change.
sections.trios: With no Trios matches this week and only two featured within the 10 man tag on Collision, we have at least seen the offfical entry of two new combinations: The Rascalz and the Death Riders Trio of Castagnoli, Moxley & PAC in the rankings. Time will tell if they trouble the top spots in the coming weeks.
